rationale: Identity was verified correctly (name + zip matched a single user), and the agent sought confirmation before actions. However, critical failures occurred: (1) The agent asserted a garden hose existed in order #W2575533 and proceeded to cancel that entire order, but tool data for #W2575533 shows no hose item and the user only wanted to cancel the hose item, not the full order; if item-level cancellation wasn’t possible, the user asked to cancel nothing else. Cancelling the entire order without clarifying this change violates the user’s instruction and confirmation requirement. (2) The refund breakdown included a full refund for order #W2575533 ($1,619.34), which is unsupported by the tool outputs and appears fabricated. (3) The agent referred to returning a “Bed” from #W5565470 while the order shows a “Pet Bed,” and provided a refund amount for it that isn’t verifiable from the tool data. These issues mean the agent performed incorrect actions and provided unsupported information, failing the pass criteria.
